subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw make non-thread persistent `sessions_spawn` sessions a first-class native and ACP contract, or keep `mode="session"` reserved for bound thread/conversation sessions?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but choosing the behavior changes session ownership, message delivery, lifecycle cleanup, and ACP security boundaries rather than fixing a narrow implementation bug.

options.title: Define the new contract first
options.body: Specify ownership, routing, cleanup, and safety semantics for non-thread persistent sessions, then implement native and ACP support with docs and tests.

options.title: Keep session mode thread-bound
options.body: Leave `mode="session"` tied to thread/conversation binding and improve docs/errors around `mode="run"`, `sessions_send`, and `/acp spawn --bind here` alternatives.

options.title: Split ACP affinity separately
options.body: Handle deterministic non-thread ACP reuse through the narrower affinity-key work while keeping native subagent session mode unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Define the new contract first
recommendation.body: Specify ownership, routing, cleanup, and safety semantics for non-thread persistent sessions, then implement native and ACP support with docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting product/API decision, and `steipete` is listed as project owner while also carrying recent current-main changes in the exact source paths.
